You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm/boot/dts/at91-sama5d2_icp.dts`**
   - Removed the line `regulator-always-on;` from the `VDD_OTHER` regulator configuration. This change indicates that the VDD_OTHER regulator will not be kept enabled at all times.

### Relationships

The modification in the device tree source file (`at91-sama5d2_icp.dts`) addresses a bug related to the VDD_OTHER regulator. The original configuration kept the regulator always enabled, which was unnecessary since VDD_OTHER is not connected to any onboard consumer. By removing the `regulator-always-on;` directive, the patch ensures that the regulator is only enabled when needed, thus optimizing power management and fixing the identified issue. This change is linked to a previous commit that added the SAMA5D2-ICP device support, indicating that the current patch is a corrective measure for that earlier implementation.

Here is the commit message:
ARM: dts: at91: sama5d2_icp: don't keep vdd_other enabled all
 the time

VDD_OTHER is not connected to any on board consumer thus it is not
needed to keep it enabled all the time.

Fixes: 68a95ef72cef ("ARM: dts: at91: sama5d2-icp: add SAMA5D2-ICP")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220826083927.3107272-9-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the unnecessary configuration of the VDD_OTHER regulator to be always enabled, despite it not being connected to any onboard consumer. This led to inefficient power management as the regulator remained active when it was not needed.

Here is the patch:
 					regulator-initial-mode = <2>;
 					regulator-allowed-modes = <2>, <4>;
-					regulator-always-on;
 
 					regulator-state-standby {

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```plaintext
-					regulator-always-on;
```
Reason:
The presence of the `regulator-always-on` configuration causes the VDD_OTHER regulator to remain enabled at all times, even though it is not connected to any onboard consumer. This results in unnecessary power consumption and inefficient power management.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```plaintext
-					regulator-always-on;
```
Reason:
Removing the `regulator-always-on` configuration allows the VDD_OTHER regulator to be disabled when not in use, thus improving power efficiency by ensuring that the regulator is only active when needed.
